title: Umag with a Dog 2027: Beaches, Rules, Costs & Best Months
metaDescription: Umag with a dog in 2027: dog beaches in the resorts, old town and restaurant rules, pet fees of €5–18 per night, summer heat, vets and EU entry rules.
content:
## Dog Beaches in Umag
Umag has no municipal beach officially signposted as a "plaža za pse" in the town centre. Dog access is organised through the resort and camp areas. Dogs are accepted on the beaches inside the camps and resorts of Park Umag, Finida, Pineta, Kanegra, Stella Maris and Savudrija. Listings also name the Laguna beach in the Stella Maris complex, the beach in the Sol Polynesia complex at Katoro, and the Savudrija beaches near the lighthouse. The Savudrija beach is described as having showers, shade and waste bins.

Policies differ between operators and change by season. Confirm access for your specific beach when booking. One listing says Camping Park Umag does not accept dogs, while regional tourism pages include its beach on the dog-friendly list. That conflict is a reason to ask before you pay.

### Are dogs allowed on other beaches in Umag?
Under the general Croatian approach, a beach without a "no dogs" sign is not formally closed to dogs. In practice, bathers complain and municipal rules often restrict dogs on public town beaches. Do not assume the central pebble and rock beaches are open to dogs. Treat them as no-go unless a sign says otherwise. Dogs on designated beaches should be on a leash, with waste bags and water carried by the owner.

> Opinion: The most common mistake is booking a central apartment and expecting to walk to a dog beach. The dog-friendly beaches sit in resort complexes about 3 km or more from the old town. A base at Katoro, Stella Maris or Savudrija works better than a flat in the centre.

## Old Town, Restaurants and Cafés
Umag's old town is a small peninsula of narrow lanes. Leashed dogs can walk the lanes and the seafront promenade without trouble. Stone paving gets hot in July and August, so walk early or after 19:00. Many restaurants and cafés with outdoor terraces tolerate a dog lying under the table. Indoor dining is usually off limits, because Croatian food-hygiene rules restrict animals in food areas. Ask before sitting down, and choose terraces in shade. Hotel and resort restaurants in Stella Maris and Kanegra are reported to accept dogs in some areas.

## National Parks, Ferries and Catamarans
Umag has no national park within its borders. Park rules also differ widely. Plitvice Lakes does not admit dogs, while some other parks allow leashed dogs on selected trails. Check each park's website before driving. Closer to Umag, the coastal path toward Savudrija and the Mirna valley roads suit dog walks without any permit. Umag has no regular domestic ferry service. Seasonal catamaran links to Trieste or Venice operate from Istrian ports. Their pet rules (carrier, muzzle, leash, fee) are set by each operator and should be confirmed in writing at booking.

## What Accommodation Charges for a Dog
Pet fees in Umag run from nothing to €60 per night. Typical figures reported for the area:
- Resort apartments in the Plava Laguna portfolio (Polynesia, Amfora, Garden Suites, Istrian Villas): about €16–18 per pet per night.
- Private apartments and villas: €5–13 per night, with Villa Ela at €5 and Apartments Ivas at €7.
- Petram Resort & Residences: €60 per pet per night, up to 2 pets.
- Some small hosts charge nothing.

The reported average among hotels with a fee is about €12 per night. A week costs roughly €35–125 for the dog. Some hosts limit the number or size of pets, so confirm this before paying a deposit.

## Summer Heat and Best Months
July and August regularly bring daytime highs around 29–32 °C. Sand and asphalt get far hotter than the air. Short-nosed breeds, seniors and dark-coated dogs struggle most. Never leave a dog in a parked car. The best months are May, June and mid-to-late September, when the sea is already swimmable and temperatures are around 20–26 °C. April and October suit walking holidays but are too cold for most dogs to swim. In peak season, walk before 09:00 and after 19:00, and carry fresh water and a collapsible bowl.

## Vet Basics
Umag has local veterinary practices, and larger clinics are in Poreč and Pula. Emergency out-of-hours care is limited, so save the number of the nearest 24-hour clinic before you travel. Istria has ticks and sand flies. Ask your own vet about tick prevention and leishmaniasis protection before travelling. Pack the vaccination record, any regular medication and a printed copy of the passport.

## EU Pet Passport Rules for Driving In
Croatia is an EU member, and the standard EU pet-travel rules apply:
- Microchip (ISO), implanted before the rabies vaccination.
- Valid rabies vaccination, given at least 21 days before travel.
- EU pet passport, or an animal health certificate for dogs from outside the EU (for example the UK).
- Maximum 5 pets per traveller on a non-commercial trip.
- Dogs should be at least 12 weeks old for vaccination, so puppies under about 15 weeks cannot travel.

A tapeworm treatment is not required for Croatia, but it is needed for Finland, Ireland, Malta and Norway. Routes via Slovenia or Italy follow the same EU rules. Non-EU residents should check current border requirements before departure.

## Verdict: How Dog-Friendly Is Umag?
Umag rates about 3.5 out of 5. Resort beaches, shaded promenades, tolerant terraces and affordable apartment fees make it easy for dogs and their owners. The weak points are the lack of a public town dog beach and the 3 km or more separation between the old town and the dog beaches. Book in or near Stella Maris, Katoro or Savudrija, travel in May, June or September, and Umag works well for a dog holiday.

faq.question: Does Umag have an official dog beach?
faq.answer: Umag has no public town beach officially marked for dogs. Dog access is provided on the beaches inside the Stella Maris, Sol Polynesia, Savudrija, Kanegra, Finida and Pineta resort areas. Confirm each beach's policy when booking.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed in Umag restaurants?
faq.answer: Dogs are generally accepted on outdoor terraces if leashed. Indoor dining areas are usually off limits under food-hygiene rules. Ask staff before sitting.

faq.question: How much does it cost to stay with a dog in Umag?
faq.answer: Most pet fees fall between €5 and €18 per night. Resort apartments commonly charge about €16–18, while private hosts often charge €5–13. A few properties charge €60 per night, and some charge nothing.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Umag with a dog?
faq.answer: May, June and mid-to-late September are the best months. Sea temperatures allow swimming, and daytime temperatures stay around 20–26 °C. July and August can exceed 30 °C and are hard on dogs.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to enter Croatia by car?
faq.answer: A dog needs a microchip, a valid rabies vaccination given at least 21 days before travel, and an EU pet passport. Dogs from outside the EU, such as the UK, need an animal health certificate instead. Customs may check these documents at the border.

faq.question: Can I take my dog on a ferry or catamaran from Umag?
faq.answer: Umag has no regular domestic ferry. Seasonal catamarans to Trieste or Venice leave from Istrian ports, and each operator sets its own pet rules. Check carrier, muzzle and fee requirements before booking.

quickAnswer: Umag is moderately dog-friendly. Dogs are welcome on beaches inside the Stella Maris, Polynesia, Savudrija, Kanegra, Finida and Pineta resort areas. The old town and most restaurant terraces accept leashed dogs. Pet fees run about €5–18 per night. Come in May, June or late September. Entry needs a microchip, a rabies vaccination and a pet passport.
